style.notes: Plain, blunt, slightly rushed. Short declarative sentences. No flattery, no scene-setting, no abstractions, no adjectives that cannot be checked. Never open by describing what the company does back to them. Never restate a fact from their funding announcement or homepage. Write like someone who looked at the product for ten minutes and has one thing to say about it.

Built an automated sourcing pipeline using LLMs and Python

blocks.label: Intent, credential, link
blocks.text: I am reaching out because I want to move from evaluating companies to building inside one.
blocks.guidance:
SENTENCE 1 -- the credential and what it taught you. Cite ONE credential from the allowed facts that best explains your observation about this company.
Then a comma, then 'and', then ONE plain finding from doing that work.
The finding must be something that went WRONG or was HARDER than expected. A difficulty you admit is credible; a competence you assert is not.

SENTENCE 2 -- the link. Choose ONE of these moves and write it in that shape. There is no default; pick the one that fits what you just said.
  at_proper_scale   "<company> is that same problem at proper scale."
  other_side        "<company> is that same problem from the other side."
  buyer_side        "That is your thesis from the buyer's side."
  solved_properly   "<company> is solving that properly; mine was <your crude version>."
  named_component   "<their named product> is that same idea applied to <X>."
  bare              No third sentence at all. Stop after the finding.
"which is why I wanted to write" is OPTIONAL and belongs to at most one of these. Do not append it by default.

HARD BANS. Breaking any of these makes the draft unusable:
- Do not begin any sentence with 'Your', 'Having', or the company name followed by praise.
- Write the company name entirely in lower case, including at the start of a sentence: "shiplog is that same idea", never "Shiplog is that same idea".
- Do not write the finding as "<thing> was <bad>; I ended up <doing Y>". That shape has been used repeatedly and now reads as a template. Vary the sentence structure, not just the nouns.
- Only state experience that appears in the allowed facts. If a fact you want is not listed, choose a different credential rather than describing work you have not done.
- Do not use: resonates, uniquely positioned, particularly compelling, particularly interesting, stands out, powerful vision, I understand the complexities, could be valuable, significant, leverage, alignment.
- Do not mention their funding round, their investors, their launch date, their headcount, or their headquarters.
- Do not use em dashes or en dashes anywhere.
- Do not use a construction that announces a lesson ('the thing that worked was', 'what I learned was', 'this taught me').
- Do not exceed three sentences or 60 words total.

blocks.label: The ask
blocks.guidance:
Write EXACTLY ONE sentence as ONE paragraph.

REPRODUCE THIS PREFIX CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER:
I am seeking a part-time role alongside my studies: I am cheap, driven and believe I could aid

Then ONE space, then a short noun phrase naming what this specific company is actually building or changing, then a full stop.
Examples of the ending only: 'the move away from segments.' / 'the rebuild of the inbox.' / 'the creation of a real AI colleague.' / 'the push into verified data.'
Four to eight words. Lower case unless it is a proper noun. Never write 'your mission' - naming the thing is the entire point of this sentence.
Do not add any other sentence, clause, or qualifier.
